grades.quote: Most memory accesses will refer to page numbers present in the TLB, and so the MMU will be able to produce the corresponding page frame number without needing to access the page table.
grades.reason: Explains that the TLB is a small cache of virtual-to-physical translations and that a TLB miss just means the translation is absent, so the page table in memory must be consulted. It never mentions disk or page faults, so it only partly answers the question.

grades.quote: The operating system software looks up the missing address translation in the page table, loads the translation into the TLB using a special instruction, and resumes normal execution.
grades.reason: Describes how a TLB miss is resolved. Either a hardware page table walker or OS software looks up the translation in the in-memory page table and loads it into the TLB. This shows that a miss is a translation-cache refill and not a disk read. It gives concrete IA-32 and MIPS examples but never mentions disk.
Describes the LoongArch TLBRD instruction, which reads a TLB entry into CSRs. It says nothing about TLB-miss handling or about disk paging.

grades.quote: Only when a new page number is accessed is the page table (of whatever kind) accessed.
grades.reason: Gives auxiliary context on how the TLB caches translations and when page table lookups happen, using linear and multilevel page tables. It implies that a TLB miss leads to a page table lookup, but it does not address disk or why no disk read is needed.
